newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks expected to maintain firm tone.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks expected to maintain firm tone.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to maintain a firm tone Tuesday, but with their upside limited due to a lack of fresh buying factors, brokers said.
They said they expect moderate buying in leading export-orientated issues, backed by the slightly weaker yen against the dollar, and in some issues that have lagged recently.
On Monday, the 225-share Nikkei average ended up 81.21 points, or 0.40 percent, at 20,604.96. Its September futures ended flat at 20,570.
"The market lacks factors to trade on, but the weaker yen may encourage buying of blue-chip exporters," said Yasuo Ueki, general manager at Nikko Securities Co Ltd.
He expects the Nikkei 225 average to trade between 20,500 and 20,800.
"Sentiment is basically firm, as there will be no credit tightening for a while and people want to buy stocks on dips," said Tatsuo Miwa, general manager at Tokai Maruman Securities Co Ltd.
